topic: Could a penny dropped from the Empire State Building kill you
hook: What if you dropped a penny from the top of the Empire State Building?

captions.hook_line: Could a penny dropped from the Empire State Building kill someone? Physics says no 🪙
captions.body: A penny is light and flat, so it tumbles, and air resistance caps its speed at roughly 50 mph. It would sting, not kill.
captions.share_line: Send this to the friend who still believes the penny myth.

youtube_title: Could a Falling Penny Kill You?

sources.claim: A falling penny tops out near 50 mph and its impact is not deadly
A penny dropped from 381 m would hurt but not kill

visual_style: Photorealistic cinematic film still, natural daylight, real materials and textures, shallow depth of field

blocks.narration: What if you dropped a penny from the top of the Empire State Building? Most people think it could kill someone below.
blocks.visual: Close-up of a hand holding a shiny copper penny over the railing of a skyscraper observation deck, the streets of New York tiny far below

shots.visual: Close-up of a hand holding a shiny copper penny over the railing of a skyscraper observation deck, the streets of New York tiny far below
shots.action: The fingers open and the penny drops away toward the street; the camera tilts down to follow it

shots.visual: Dramatic view straight down the side of a tall Art Deco skyscraper to the busy Manhattan streets far below
shots.action: The camera plunges down the face of the building toward the street, wind rushing past

shots.visual: A man in a gray wool coat walking along a busy New York sidewalk, seen from slightly above
shots.action: He walks along unaware while a tiny copper glint falls toward him from above; the camera pushes in

blocks.narration: But a penny is flat. It tumbles like a leaf, and air resistance caps its speed at only about fifty miles an hour.
blocks.visual: Macro close-up of a copper penny tumbling in midair against a blurred blue sky

shots.visual: Macro close-up of a copper penny tumbling in midair against a blurred blue sky
shots.action: The penny flips and flutters edge over edge like a falling leaf, catching the sunlight, in slow motion

shots.visual: A copper penny falling past the windows of a skyscraper, faint white wisps of air streaming up around it
shots.action: Wisps of air push up against the penny and its fall steadies instead of speeding up

blocks.narration: Physicists say it would sting, but not kill. The person below would just rub their head, look up, and wonder:
blocks.visual: Close-up of the shoulder of a gray wool coat on a New York sidewalk, a copper penny just about to land on it

shots.visual: Close-up of the shoulder of a gray wool coat on a New York sidewalk, a copper penny just about to land on it
shots.action: The penny bounces off the shoulder and rolls away across the pavement; the man flinches slightly

shots.visual: The same man in the gray wool coat on the sidewalk, rubbing his head and looking up at a towering Art Deco skyscraper
shots.action: He rubs his head and squints upward; the camera tilts up the skyscraper into the bright sky
